findings.statement: CA9 is the top convergence gene: RNA up [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.31] and protein up [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.27], with strong RNA-protein agreement [gene=CA9; type=omics_rna_protein_correlation; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; spearman_rho=0.797]. It replicates in TCGA-KIRC, survives purity extrapolation, is a membrane enzyme with antibody drugs (girentuximab), but is not prognostic in TCGA.

CD70 is up in tumour at RNA [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=4.46] and protein [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.42], replicates in TCGA-KIRC, and is not tissue-enriched in vital organs [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34], so it has the cleanest safety profile among the top surface targets; clinical-stage antibody and CAR-T agents exist. No selective DepMap dependency and no prognostic signal.

SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile (tumour-up RNA and protein, TCGA replication, tumour-intrinsic by purity), but the vital-organ proteome shows adrenal enrichment, a safety concern [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08]. No approved drug is attached to it in the graph.

NNMT is up in tumour RNA [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=4.67] and in protein, replicates in TCGA-KIRC, is tumour-intrinsic by purity, and higher expression is associated with worse survival in TCGA (significant Cox). It is top-ranked in the biomarker profile among tumour-up genes.

Negative result for NNMT druggability: the PRISM screen shows no selective ccRCC sensitivity for the only annotated compound (niacin, with multiple targets) [gene=NNMT; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; padj=0.599], and DepMap gives no selective dependency.

ENPP3 is a tumour-up surface enzyme that ranks high in the target profile, with RNA and protein increase, TCGA-KIRC replication, tumour-intrinsic signal and an antibody-drug conjugate (AGS-16C3F, phase 2) already in the graph. Vital-organ safety was not queried.

SLC16A3 (MCT4) is up in tumour at RNA and protein, replicates in TCGA-KIRC, and has a real cis copy-number effect; it has no selective ccRCC dependency and only borderline prognostic signal in TCGA, so it is a metabolic-hypoxia marker more than a validated target.

FCER1G (and TYROBP) look tumour-up in bulk, but this is largely immune infiltration: expression tracks purity inversely [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692] and the RNA fold change extrapolated to a pure tumour shrinks to [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.061]. It is an immune-content marker, not a tumour-cell target.

VHL is the disease driver: recurrently mutated [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483], with 3p loss [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791], and a positive cis copy-number effect on RNA, i.e. a real dosage effect. Loss of VHL stabilises HIF and explains the CA9, NNMT and hypoxia-gene (SLC16A3, HILPDA) induction. VHL itself changes little at RNA or protein, so it is not a DE biomarker.

PSAT1 is the top biomarker-profile gene but it is down in tumour (loss of normal tubule metabolism) at RNA and protein, replicates in TCGA-KIRC, and low expression is associated with worse survival (significant Cox); it is a prognostic tissue biomarker, not a target.

ALDOB is strongly down in tumour at RNA and protein, replicates in TCGA-KIRC, tracks proximal-tubule identity loss, and low expression is associated with worse survival; a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker, not a target.

UMOD has an extreme RNA loss in tumour (largest fold change in the top-ranked set), protein loss, and TCGA replication, reflecting loss of thick-ascending-limb identity; useful as a tumour-vs-normal tissue marker but not prognostic and not a target.

caveats: Normal-tissue safety was queried only for CA9, CD70 and SCARB1; the GTEx proteome has no kidney, so kidney on-target toxicity is untested.
DepMap/PRISM 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 biology; no top gene shows a selective ccRCC dependency, so target claims rest on expression, surface localisation and existing drugs.

Convergence scores include literature and tractability streams that can favour well-studied genes; only a subset of candidates had purity, mutation and phosphosite layers checked, and no kinase activity was reviewed.
CPTAC bulk samples contain immune and stromal cells; immune genes (FCER1G, TYROBP) are likely infiltration signals.
Findings are cross-sectional associations (110 tumours; 75 RNA and 84 proteome normals), not causal.
